extracted.intended_audience: high-school journalism students and student-newspaper staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for student journalists on reviewing films, reporting musical performances, and writing newspaper columns; emphasizes factual reporting, appropriate technical comment, ethical tone, and craft-specific evaluation points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectivity and factuality in musical reports
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be no vague generalities. The reader is primarily interested in facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give an objective report within your limitations and add impressions that are to the point and grounded in the facts of the performance. Emphasize concrete information over vague commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate technical comment
rubrics_metrics.description: He should be able to infuse just enough technical comment into his story to give it reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include technical detail when it enhances realism, but calibrate it so both the enthusiast and the non-technical reader can follow (analogous to a sports writer using vernacular to enliven a story).

rubrics_metrics.name: Include program-specific information
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever specific information from the program will interest readers, should be presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report items such as works performed, composers, soloists, notable program choices, and any program details that will interest the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form follows purpose: news vs. feature
rubrics_metrics.description: The principles of news writing hold if the report is straight news. The principles of feature writing hold if the performance is of a nature to be best presented as a feature story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether the performance warrants a straightforward news account or a feature approach and apply the appropriate conventions and structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selectivity — highlight the high points
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot write up the facts of the whole concert. Select the high lights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When constrained by space, choose and expand on the most important or memorable moments rather than attempting an exhaustive blow-by-blow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Musical-performance technical criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate attacks, balance and blend of tone, modulation of crescendos, smoothness of texture, tonal volume, responsiveness to the leader, and register balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specific musical vocabulary to assess ensemble discipline (attack, blend, balance, dynamics, phrasing) with examples (e.g., soloists standing out, lack of blend, effective pianissimo).

rubrics_metrics.name: Repertoire variety and demonstration of versatility
rubrics_metrics.description: They had little opportunity to show how versatile a chorus they were, for only one type of music was on their program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge ensembles on the range and appropriateness of repertoire; a varied program better demonstrates versatility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language choice and impact on musicality
rubrics_metrics.description: Sung in English... the translated text had the effect of hamstringing Mozart's inspired cavatina.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether translations or performing language harm musical phrasing, flow, or idiomatic expression; comment on effect of language choice on musicality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographic and visual/cinematography quality
rubrics_metrics.description: There are some exquisite photographic bits — truly lovely reproductions of the beauty of tropical nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate cinematography, composition, lighting, photographic effects and how visuals contribute to the film's impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acting quality and star appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Monte Blue's work is marked by sincerity and restraint... a poor film made enjoyable by the acting or popularity of a film star.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess actors for sincerity, restraint, diction (in talkies), and how star presence influences audience reception; note standout performances or audience reactions (e.g., hissing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity of cultural portrayal
rubrics_metrics.description: The natives are absolutely naive and natural and the hula-hula dancing and other native entertainment and customs, presumably, are the genuine article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the authenticity and sensitivity of cultural representation: are customs and performances believable and respectfully depicted?

rubrics_metrics.name: Direction and overall production leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: W. S. Van Dyke... should receive all sorts of medals and blue ribbons for having produced a remarkable and compelling picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the director's control of tone, pacing, performances, visual style, and the cohesiveness of the production as a whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story strength and construction
rubrics_metrics.description: The story ... is strong and well put together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess plot coherence, pacing, adaptation fidelity (when based on a novel/play), and how well story elements are organized and resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound-film diction and synchronization
rubrics_metrics.description: Note also the diction of the actors and the timing of the action with the sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For talking films, evaluate clarity of speech, accent issues, and how well audio cues and dialogue are synchronized with on-screen action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles and intertitles effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Review a film in which you play up the cleverness of the titles or their lack of punch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe whether titles/intertitles (or modern equivalents) enhance tone, humor, or comprehension; poor titles can undercut musical or dramatic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent assessment and comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Go to a picture and write a review of it without reading what the press has to say. Compare afterward for points of similarity and of difference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form your own judgment first, then compare with others to learn about differing emphases and critical standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Columnist reliability, judgment, and temperament
rubrics_metrics.description: Students clamor for the editorship, but they must demonstrate their reliability, good judgment, and kindly attitude to their fellows ... before they are capable of this responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial/column responsibilities should be entrusted to those who show sound judgment, consistency, and a temperate, considerate demeanor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Column originality, first-hand material and timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Use first-hand material. Life about you furnishes the best fabric for humor. Be timely. The pun is the lowest form of wit. Don't clip jokes from other periodicals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor original, timely, first-hand observations over recycled material; seek fresh angles and avoid lazy devices like puns or wholesale clipping of jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Column tone: tasteful, non-vulgar, and charitable
rubrics_metrics.description: Blessed are the clean of heart. Nothing coarse or vulgar should ever appear. Never joke about a personal matter that is half true; it may hurt. Nor hold up to ridicule what others regard as sacred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep humor clean and avoid content that humiliates individuals or attacks sacred beliefs; prioritize kindness and avoid cheap assaults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange-column etiquette and constructive criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: In your exchange column don't criticize the faults of your exchanges. There must be something in a paper from Detroit or Kalamazoo that interests you ... Remember that the student staff, like yours, is most likely in earnest. A sharp thrust from a 'smart-aleck' exchange is discourteous and perhaps even discouraging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When commenting on other student papers, be constructive and look for genuinely interesting or unusual items rather than lampooning peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Column format suitability for high-school papers
rubrics_metrics.description: For the high school paper a column of short items of many varieties is usually more satisfactory than a continuous column on one subject, unless, of course, a student with the rare gift of humor is on the staff. Slip cuts help a humor column.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer a short-items format for variety and reader interest in school papers; use slip cuts and brief items to sustain attention unless a singularly gifted columnist can carry a continuous column.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience-appropriate register
rubrics_metrics.description: Just as the sports writer uses enough of the vernacular to make his account live for the enthusiast as well as for the reader who has no technical knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust language and technicality to serve both knowledgeable enthusiasts and general readers—use enough specialized terms to be authentic but explain or temper them for lay readers.
